messages.content: "Imagine you are a sculptor working on a large project. You have two different types of materials available to you, each with a different density. The first material has a density of 5.2 g/cm^3 and the second material has a density of 7.8 g/cm^3. You are planning to create two identical cones, each with a base radius of 10 cm and a height of 30 cm. The first cone will be made from the first material and the second cone will be made from the second material. Can you calculate the volume of each cone, rounding off to 2 decimal places, and then calculate the mass of each cone using their respective densities?"

function.name: geometry_calculate_cone_volume

function.name: physics_calculate_cone_mass
function.description: Calculate the mass of a cone given the radius, height, and density. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

radius.description: Radius of the cone base. This is a float type value.

height.description: Height of the cone. This is a float type value.

density.description: Density of the material the cone is made of. This is a float type value.

message.content:
**Volumes**

Both cones share the same size:
\[
V=\frac{1}{3}\pi r^{\,2}h=
   \frac{1}{3}\,\pi(10)^2(30)
   =\frac{1}{3}\,\pi(3000)=1000\pi
   \approx 3141.59~{\rm cm}^{3}
\]

Rounded to **two decimal places**,  
\(V_{\text{cone}} = 3141.59~{\rm cm}^{3}\).

---

### Cone A – Material Density \(5.2~{\rm g/cm^{3}}\)

\[
m_A = \rho_A V 
     = 5.2\times 3141.59
     \approx 16\,336.27~{\rm g}
\]
Rounded to two decimals: **\(m_A = 16\,336.27~{\rm g}\)**.

---

### Cone B – Material Density \(7.8~{\rm g/cm^{3}}\)

\[
m_B = \rho_B V 
     = 7.8\times 3141.59
     \approx 24\,504.41~{\rm g}
\]
Rounded to two decimals: **\(m_B = 24\,504.41~{\rm g}\)**.

So,

| Cone | Volume (\({\rm cm}^{3}\)) | Mass (\({\rm g}\)) |
|------|--------------------------|--------------------|
| A    | 3141.59                  | 16 336.27          |
| B    | 3141.59                  | 24 504.41          |

These figures give you the required rounded‑off volumes and corresponding masses based on each material’s density.
